Pavlovo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zakarpattia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. The first Jews arrived in Pavlovo in the 18th century, growing from 3 people in 1851 to 71 by 1880 and 134 by 1930. Following the March 1939 Hungarian occupation, Jews were persecuted and forced out of their occupations; some were drafted into forced labor battalions or sent to the Eastern Front, where most perished. In 1941, Jews without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to German-occupied Kamianets-Podilskyi and shot, and the remaining Jews of Pavlovo were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. The house of the Hisser family, killed at Auschwitz, is a Greek Catholic church today.
